t: The Almoravids came to al-Andalus at the request of taifa rulers such as Al-Mu'tamid of Seville, after Alfonso VI took Toledo in 1085 and pressed on the other taifas.
Yusuf ibn Tashfin kept an elite reserve hidden behind a mound and attacked the Castilian camp while Alfonso's troops were pursuing the Andalusian line, and Alfonso broke off to save his camp.
Within about eighteen months of the battle the Almoravids had conquered the major cities of al-Andalus and ended the era of the taifa kings.
dyk: The Muslim army is said to have brought camels from Morocco whose sight and sound frightened the Castilian horses, and Arabic sources call the field az-Zallaqah, 'slippery ground', after the bloodshed there.
ev: Al-Mu'tamid ibn Abbad of Seville writes to Yusuf ibn Tashfin asking for help against Alfonso VI
Alfonso VI captures Toledo, which Muslims had held for 372 years, and takes lands along the Tagus
Yusuf ibn Tashfin takes Algeciras as his base and crosses into al-Andalus with his army
Alfonso VI proposes fighting on a Monday, and the armies camp either side of the Wadi Bira
The Muslim army defeats Alfonso VI at Sagrajas, and he escapes to Coria after dark
Yusuf ibn Tashfin returns to besiege Aledo and withdraws after four months
Yusuf ibn Tashfin crosses a third time and besieges Toledo, then lifts the siege for lack of supplies
Almoravid armies capture Córdoba, and Seville falls, ending the rule of the taifa kings

f.date: 23 October 1086 (Friday, 12 Rajab 479 AH); Muslim sources say Alfonso VI had agreed to fight on the Monday
f.place: The plain of Zallaqa or Sagrajas, north of Badajoz near the present border of Portugal, in the west of the Iberian Peninsula
f.sides: The Almoravids under Yusuf ibn Tashfin and the taifa forces under Al-Mu'tamid ibn Abbad of Seville, with ten thousand Almoravid cavalry in the vanguard and 4,000 black troops among the Almoravids; Alfonso VI of Castile with allies from Aragon and elsewhere, his army put at 60,000
f.outcome: The Muslim forces won and Alfonso VI fled by night to Coria. The sieges of major Andalusian cities were lifted, and Yusuf ibn Tashfin's standing in al-Andalus rose.
